verdict: B 44.2 / Discard (3 gates failed: role honesty, statistical, FF5)
lesson: Adaptive IC-weighted factor rotation with expanding-window ICIR and 2-month lag is PIT-clean but delivers zero FF5 alpha in Korean market (t=-0.03). The 2-month IC lag necessary for strict C14 PIT compliance appears to destroy any IC predictability signal (Asness 2016 factor timing literature assumes monthly availability). Korean market IC-rotation faces structural headwinds: (1) IC itself is noisy (short cross-section ~800 stocks), (2) factor premia shift faster than expanding ICIR can capture, (3) ICIR deactivation threshold (0.1) may be too generous. VT 15% + DD 8/20 overlay provides decent MDD control (23.38%) but cannot create alpha where the base signal has none. OOS retention 0.54 confirms in-sample overfitting of ICIR weights. Arnott et al. 2019 'Alice in Factorland' warns that factor timing adds noise in small markets. Prefer regime-conditional static weights (STR_1433 approach) over continuous IC-based rotation for KR equity.
